newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgians spending less on food, more on leisure.
newsitem.headline: Belgians spending less on food, more on leisure.

text.p: The average Belgian household spends proportionally less money on food than a decade ago but more on leisure and transport, according to a survey released on Friday by the country's National Statistics Institute.
Data provided by 2,724 households from June 1995 to end-May 1996 showed that on average each spent one million Belgian francs ($29,200) over the 12-month period.
Spending on food represented 13.4 percent of the total, down from 15.1 percent 10 years earlier and 17.7 percent 20 years before.
Personal transport took up a 10-percent share, a rise from 8.7 percent a decade before when the previous survey was carried out.
Culture, learning and leisure activities accounted for 8.1 percent, up from 7.5 percent, while the share of spending on restaurants, days out and holidays rose to 8.2 percent from 7.9 percent.
